title: CVE-2026-120382: Critical Synology DSM OAuth Flaw Enables Arbitrary File Access
content_md: Synology has disclosed a critical vulnerability affecting DiskStation Manager (DSM) and BeeStation OS that can allow unauthenticated remote attackers to read or write arbitrary files and trigger denial-of-service conditions. Tracked as CVE-2026-120382, the flaw resides in the OAuth API and carries a CVSS 3.1 score of 9.8, Critical . The vulnerability is classified as CWE-88: Improper Neutralization of Argument Delimiters in a Command . According to Synology, the affected OAuth API fails to properly neutralize command argument delimiters, allowing attacker-controlled input to alter how a downstream command interprets its parameters. No authentication or user interaction is required. The issue is particularly serious for organizations exposing Synology NAS management services to untrusted networks. Successful exploitation could expose confidential files stored on the NAS, allow attackers to modify or replace files, or disrupt device availability. Synology’s official advisory does not currently state that the vulnerability directly enables arbitrary command execution or remote code execution, so the confirmed impact should be limited to the vendor-documented file read/write and denial-of-service capabilities. Contact Sales The vulnerability affects multiple DSM generations as well as BeeStation OS 1.5. Synology recommends updating supported installations as soon as fixed builds become available and deactivating the OAuth Service package as an immediate workaround. As of November
